Prebuilt **Linux and Windows x86-64** binaries of `k3`, the pure-C Kimi K3 inference
engine from [FareedKhan-dev/kimi-k3-in-c](https://github.com/FareedKhan-dev/kimi-k3-in-c),
**built with the Tiny C Compiler (TCC) only**.

This release changes how k3 is built. The engine's features and output are the same as
[v1.1.0-win.1](https://github.com/s81/kimi-work-8Gb/releases/tag/v1.1.0-win.1): every
test checks that the results match bit for bit. The whole build is now a single command:

```
tcc -run build.c [test | dist]
```

That replaces make, CMake, GCC, MinGW/MSYS2, shell scripts and Python. It works the same
on Linux and Windows.

> **Read this before upgrading: compute is about 14x slower.** TCC has no SIMD and does
> little optimisation, so the kernels use their scalar code paths. If you need speed,
> stay on [v1.1.0-win.1](https://github.com/s81/kimi-work-8Gb/releases/tag/v1.1.0-win.1)
> (Windows, GCC AVX2), or build upstream with GCC. The numbers are under *Performance*
> below.

## Downloads

| File | Runs on |
|---|---|
| `k3-1.2.0-windows-x64.zip` | 64-bit Windows Vista or later, any x86-64 CPU |
| `k3-1.2.0-linux-x64.zip` | 64-bit Linux with glibc 2.38 or newer (e.g. Ubuntu 24.04, Debian 13, Fedora 39), any x86-64 CPU |
| `SHA256SUMS.txt` | Checksums for both zips |

Each zip contains `k3` (`k3.exe` on Windows), `LICENSE`, `NOTICE` and `README.txt`.

- **No installer and no extra DLLs.**
  - `k3.exe` imports only `kernel32.dll` and `msvcrt.dll`, which ship with Windows.
  - The Linux `k3` needs only `libc.so.6` and `libm.so.6`.
- **One build per OS, no CPU variants.** These builds have no AVX2 code, so they run on
  any 64-bit x86 CPU and can't fail with an illegal-instruction error.
- **Verify the download.**
  - PowerShell: `Get-FileHash .\k3-1.2.0-windows-x64.zip -Algorithm SHA256`
  - Linux: `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS.txt --ignore-missing`
- **Quick check:** `k3 --version` should print `k3 1.2.0`. `k3 --list-presets` also works
  without the model.

## You still need the model

These zips contain the engine only. Running inference needs the Kimi K3 checkpoint
(about 1.56 TB), downloaded separately. See
[docs/QUICKSTART.md](https://github.com/s81/kimi-work-8Gb/blob/v1.2.0/docs/QUICKSTART.md).
On Windows, pass non-ASCII prompts with `--prompt-file`, because Windows re-encodes argv
to the active code page.

## What changed

- **TCC-only build.** The Makefile, the CMake files and `scripts/build-windows.sh` are
  gone. `build.c` builds `k3` and the test binaries and runs the full weightless test gate,
  including the CLI refusal checks. `dist` writes the release zip itself, with a built-in
  zip writer. Every compile uses `-Wall -Werror`.
- **Own thread pool instead of OpenMP.** `src/core/k3_par.c` covers all eight former
  `#pragma omp` loops. `--threads` and `OMP_NUM_THREADS` work as before. It scales 3.65x
  (bf16) and 3.9x (MXFP4) from 1 to 4 threads.
- **Windows runtime layer in `src/compat/`.** It fills the gaps in TCC's msvcrt-based C
  runtime:
  - pthreads on native threads, with Vista condition variables;
  - `unistd.h` and `dirent.h`;
  - 64-bit `lseek`;
  - `clock_gettime`, `mkstemp` and `fma`;
  - run-time lookups for kernel32 calls added in Vista and later.
- **TCC version pinned.** This release uses TCC 0.9.28rc (TinyCC commit `e23dabed`),
  itself built from source with TCC. The official 0.9.27 Windows release miscompiles NaN
  checks (`!(x > 0.0)` behaves like `x <= 0.0`), which breaks the engine's NaN guards, so
  it isn't used.
- **Platforms.** macOS is no longer built or tested.

## Fixed

- **File offsets past 2 GB on Windows.** `off_t` is 32-bit in the Windows C runtime, so
  the shard and trunk readers wrapped every offset past 2 GB. Offsets are now `int64_t`
  and file seeks use `_lseeki64`.

Also included, unchanged from v1.1.0-win.1: the upstream trunk-report counting fix
([`7721a1b`](https://github.com/FareedKhan-dev/kimi-k3-in-c/commit/7721a1b)).

## Performance

Kernel timings at real Kimi K3 dimensions on a 4-core Xeon, three runs each:

| Kernel | GCC -O3 AVX2 (v1.1.0-win.1) | TCC (this release) |
|---|---|---|
| bf16 matmul 12288 x 7168 | 10.15 / 10.05 / 10.82 ms | 148.4 / 165.7 / 127.9 ms |
| MXFP4 matmul 3072 x 3584 | 1.29 / 0.81 / 1.31 ms | 17.32 / 19.27 / 16.81 ms |

- **Output:** both builds print the same output digests.
- **I/O:** phases limited by disk reads, which dominate low-memory presets, are
  unaffected.
- **Old figures:** the time-per-token numbers in the README and `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` were
  measured with the old GCC build.

## How it was built and verified

- Built by [`release.yml`](https://github.com/s81/kimi-work-8Gb/blob/v1.2.0/.github/workflows/release.yml)
  on GitHub's `ubuntu-latest` and `windows-latest` runners, with TCC set up by
  [`setup-tcc`](https://github.com/s81/kimi-work-8Gb/blob/v1.2.0/.github/actions/setup-tcc/action.yml).
- The same jobs ran the full weightless test suite on each OS before packaging. The
  results were `22 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped`, `VERDICT: ENGINE MATCHES THE REFERENCE
  EXACTLY` and `ALL WEIGHTLESS TESTS PASSED`. On Windows, two subtests skip by design (no
  inodes, no `fork`).
- **Not verified:** inference on real Kimi K3 weights with the TCC build, and tokenizer
  parity. Both need the checkpoint, which CI does not have.

Build it yourself: the README's *Building* section, and
[docs/BUILD-WINDOWS.md](https://github.com/s81/kimi-work-8Gb/blob/v1.2.0/docs/BUILD-WINDOWS.md).
